newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech govt approves Aero aircraft purchase.
newsitem.headline: Czech govt approves Aero aircraft purchase.

text.p: The Czech government has approved the purchase of 72 sub-sonic L-159 light fighters, developed by troubled plane maker Aero Vodochody a.s., Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus said on Wednesday.
"The government approved the decision to buy these planes," Klaus told journalists after a regular cabinet meeting.

Aero, which is looking both home and abroad for a strategic partner to help it out of a financial crisis, had a long-standing letter of intent with the Czech army for delivery of the fighters, but no final deal had been approved until now.
Klaus said the cabinet also ruled that foreign-made supersonic fighters should be purchased with the aim of having them in operation by 2003. He did not say when the L-159s should be delivered.
Aero is currently developing the L-159s with U.S.-supplied avionics. Klaus said the final contract should be ready for signing by the end of April.

The Czech government has declared it will sell a 34-40 percent stake in the troubled company to a financially strong strategic investor for a minimum of 950 million crowns ($32.4 million) through an equity expansion. The cabinet must still decide how large the stake will be.
U.S. Boeing Co, McDonnell Douglas and Czech airlines Ceske Aerolinie a.s. have submitted a joint bid for the stake.
Other parties expressing interest in the Aero tender include British Aerospace Plc and Sweden's Saab bidding as part of the "Gripen" consortium, and the Czech investment company, CIMEX Holding a.s..
Another serious Czech contender, chemical and industrial conglomerate Chemapol Group a.s. has reportedly lost interest in the firm because of Aero's severe financial problems.
-- Jan Lopatka, Prague Newsroom, 420-2-2423-0003 ($ = 29.31 Czech Crowns)
